full_judgment: 9. This section empowers a Court of appeal, confirmation, reference or revision to stay any order passed by a Court subordinate to it under sections 517, 518 or 519 Cr. P. C. and further to modify, alter or annul such order and make further orders which it may consider just. The only limitation on the exercise of such power appears from the words "pending consideration by the former Court" which occur in the section itself. To make any of the orders as aforesaid the appellate court (in the present case) must be in seisin of the matter involving an order passed by a subordinate court under any of the sections mentioned above. It cannot be said that after passing the order on July 29, 1980, which has been quoted above, in disposing of Criminal Appeal No.66 of 1980, the court was any longer in seisin of the matter. The order passed by the learned Magistrate was no longer pending consideration by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. He had obviously, therefore, no jurisdiction to pass the impugned order on September 11, 1980.
